newsitem.title: BURUNDI: Burundi army signals offensive against Hutu rebels.
newsitem.headline: Burundi army signals offensive against Hutu rebels.

text.p: Burundi's Tutsi-led army signalled on Wednesday that it was preparing an offensive against Hutu rebels after fierce clashes just south of the capital Bujumbura.
"Don't be surprised if (the fighting) continues today," said Lieutenant-Colonel Longin Minani, a Defence Ministry adviser. "We want all of them destroyed. We want to secure the population."
Hundreds of people fled their homes south of Bujumbura on Tuesday afternoon after heavy clashes between rebels and the army.
Residents in the capital heard gunfire and heavy artillery from the surrounding hills.
Minani said rebels had established themselves at Muhuta, Mutambu and Kanyosha -- three communes south of the capital -- but army was attacking their training camps.
He said the rebels, who have been fighting the Tutsi-dominated government since the first elected Hutu president was killed in 1993, had established a "parallel administration" in Kanyosha.
"They have their own governor," he said. "They ask for contributions, they collect taxes by force."
Residents fleeing the area bore green receipts stamped CNDD (National Council for the Defence of Democracy), the military wing of the Hutu rebels.
An army spokesman said on Tuesday night that government troops had killed 30 rebels and seized seven weapons in the fighting.
Minani could not say how big the rebel force was. "There were so many, that is why we used mortars," he said.
More than 150,000 people have been killed in massacres and civil war between the army and rebels since 1993.
